## core

### `core.bloch`

`src/manim_atoms/core/bloch.py` — The Bloch sphere: a two-level state, or a collective spin, as a direction.

- class `BlochView()`: A Bloch sphere drawn in perspective on a flat scene: |e> up, the viewer a little above the equator, looking down by ``elevation``.
  - `.point(v)`: Where the direction ``v`` lands on screen.
  - `.depth(v)`: > 0 for a point on the side of the sphere facing the viewer.
  - `.curve(points, color, width, back_opacity=0.35)`: A curve through directions on the sphere: solid in front, dashed and faint behind.
  - `.ring(axis, height=0.0, n=160)`: The circle of directions v with v . axis = height.
  - `.outline()`
  - `.patch(center, e1, e2, a, b, n=90)`: The outline of a patch of the sphere round the direction ``center``: an ellipse of angular half-widths ``a`` along the tangent ``e1`` and ``b`` along ``e2``, wrapped onto the surface.
- `noise_patch(view, center, e1, e2, a, b, color)`: The collective spin's quantum noise, a filled patch on the sphere.

### `core.citations`

`src/manim_atoms/core/citations.py` — A citation as a line on a slide.

- `citation(*refs, fmt=SHORT, numbered=False, font_size=FONT_CITATION, color=CITATION_COLOR, max_width=CITATION_MAX_WIDTH)`: One line per reference, left aligned, shrunk to fit ``max_width``.
- `labelled_citation(items, fmt=AUTHOR_YEAR, font_size=FONT_CITATION, color=CITATION_COLOR, max_width=CITATION_MAX_WIDTH)`: ``items`` are (label, refs) pairs, refs one reference or a list of them (Reference or LaTeX string, as for citation()): each becomes "label: refs", and they run on, separated, onto as few lines as keep within ``max_width``.
- `place_citation(mob, corner=DL)`: ``mob`` in a corner of the slide: by default the footer, bottom left, its last line just above the progress bar. The bottom right keeps clear of the slide number; on the right the lines are right aligned.

### `core.layout`

`src/manim_atoms/core/layout.py` — The furniture of a static slide: a heading, a list, a picture, a slot.

- `slide_title(text)`: A slide's heading, top left, where every animation puts its own.
- `load_image(path, height=None, width=None, lift=False)`: An image file as an ImageMobject, sized by height or width.
- `image_point(image, px, py)`: Pixel (px, py) of an ImageMobject, counted from its upper left, on screen.
- `numbered_list(items, font_size=FONT_CONTENTS, buff=0.45)`: 1. first, 2. second, ... with the numbers in a column of their own.
- `placeholder_frame(width, height, label)`: A dashed slot, labelled, for a figure that has yet to be dropped in.

### `core.optics`

`src/manim_atoms/core/optics.py` — Optics: beams drawn as Gaussian profiles, and an optical cavity.

- `gaussian_band(start, end, width, color, opacity=BEAM_OPACITY, layers=BEAM_LAYERS)`: A beam seen side on: nested bands, brightest along its axis, so it reads as a Gaussian profile rather than a flat bar.
- `gaussian_spot(center, radius, color, opacity=BEAM_OPACITY, layers=BEAM_LAYERS)`: A beam seen end on, the same way: nested discs.
- `rabi_transmission(x, center, kappa, gamma, coupling)`: The cavity's transmission at probe frequency x, with the cavity and the atoms both resonant at ``center``: |kappa / (kappa - i D + G^2/(gamma - i D))|^2 at detuning D, for cavity and atomic half-widths kappa and gamma and collective coupling G = g sqrt(N_g). One peak of height 1 for an empty cavity (G = 0); two, near center +- G, once G outgrows the widths.
- `make_cavity(center, length, mirror_height, mode_width, lead_in, lead_out)`: Two concave mirrors ``length`` apart about ``center``, the cavity mode between them, and the probe beam coming in ``lead_in`` from the left and going on ``lead_out`` to the right into a detector.

### `core.primitives`

`src/manim_atoms/core/primitives.py` — Atoms, laser pulses and the recoil they hand over: the atom-interferometry building blocks every other scene is drawn with.

- `make_atom(color=ATOM_COLOR, radius=ATOM_RADIUS, opacity=1.0)`: An atom drawn as a flat filled disc.
- `make_cloud(center, color, n=CARTOON_CLOUD_N, radius=CARTOON_CLOUD_RADIUS, seed=0)`: A still cartoon of an atom cloud: dots in a round Gaussian heap, pulled in to ``radius`` so the cloud has an edge.
- `make_laser_pulse(x, y, length=PULSE_LENGTH, n_cycles=PULSE_CYCLES)`: A Gaussian-enveloped sine wavepacket propagating along +y, centred on (x, y).
- `momentum_arrow(origin, direction, tex, label_dir=LEFT, length=1.1)`: A recoil arrow with its label, e.g. the hbar k an atom gains from a pulse.
- `grow(annotation)`: Animations that bring a momentum_arrow on screen.
- `make_k_arrow(x, y)`: The little vertical k-vector marker that sits beside a beam.
- `make_guide(start, end)`: A dashed construction line, e.g. the trajectory an atom arrives along.
- `absorb(scene, x, atom, extras=(), fade=())`: A wavepacket rises from below and is absorbed: |g, p> -> |e, p + hbar k>.
- `emit(scene, x, atom, extras=())`: Stimulated emission: one photon arrives and two leave.
- `draw_legs(scene, legs, fade=(), extra=())`: Move atoms along straight legs, drawing each trajectory in step.
- `state_colors(atom, color)`: Recolour an atom's body to match a new internal state, keeping the highlight.
- `state_label(tex, color, font_size=FONT_STATE)`: A ket or other state name as MathTex, in the lightened shade of its state's colour.
- `arm_ket(excited, phase=None, font_size=FONT_LEGEND, stacked=False)`: The state an arm is in: |g, p> or |e, p + hbar k>, in that state's colour.
- `fluorescence(atoms)`: What fluoresce plays, unplayed: (halos, the animations lighting them).
- `fluoresce(scene, atoms, fade=(), run_time=0.8)`: Atoms caught by an imaging pulse light up in its blue.
- `recoil(state, from_below)`: (velocity change in recoils, new state) for an arm in ``state`` ("g" or "e") hit by a pulse travelling up (``from_below``) or down: a |g> arm absorbs, moving with the photon; an |e> arm is stimulated to emit into the pulse, recoiling against it.
- `state_legend()`: The key to the two states: an atom in each colour beside |g, p> and |e, p + hbar k>, one above the other.

### `core.spacetime`

`src/manim_atoms/core/spacetime.py` — Space-time diagrams: worldlines, and running one on a single lab clock.

- `leg_point(start, end, disp, s)`: Where an atom on a bowed leg is, a fraction s of the way along it.
- `wavy_path(start, end, color, disp, s_max=1.0)`: The leg bowed by the wave, drawn a fraction s_max of the way along.
- `no_displacement(_)`: A quiet baseline: the legs are straight and the corners are where they say.
- `leg_share(start, end, t)`: How far along the leg from `start` to `end` lab time `t` has got.
- `run_to(scene, clock, to, *anims, **kwargs)`: Advance lab time to `to` at V, playing `anims` while it runs.
- `worldline(corners, disp=no_displacement)`: A function from lab time to where an arm is, given the corners it turns at.
- `wound(clock, rate, t_from, t_to)`: An updater for the angle an arm excited from t_from to t_to has reached.
- `growing_band(band, t_from, t_to, now, style=WINDOW_STYLE)`: A band over a stretch of the diagram, filling in as that stretch is flown.
- `wound_with_shift(clock, rate, t_from, t_to, on, off, shift)`: wound(), with `shift` accrued on top of it across the window [on, off].
- `wound_with_jumps(clock, rate, t_from, t_to, jumps)`: wound(), plus a step `delta` at each (t, delta) in `jumps` once lab time has passed t.
- `carry(atom, path, clock)`: Pin an atom to its worldline for as long as lab time is running.
- `growing_trail(corners, color, clock, disp=no_displacement)`: The trajectory behind an arm, drawn as far as lab time has got.
- `draw_wavy_legs(scene, legs, fade=(), extra=())`: draw_legs for clouds whose worldlines carry the wave's displacement.
- `along(start, end, f)`: A fraction f of the way from one corner to the next.

### `core.video`

`src/manim_atoms/core/video.py` — A recorded video shown inside a scene, one frame at a time.

- `load_video_frames(path, every=1, crop=None)`: Every ``every``-th frame of the video at ``path``, as RGBA arrays.
- class `VideoFrame(ImageMobject)`: An image whose pixels can be swapped for another frame of a video.
  - `.show(index)`: Show frame ``index``, clamped to the frames there are.

### `core.plots`

`src/manim_atoms/core/plots.py` — Plots drawn in manim: log-log axes, and scatters of thousands of dots.

- `log_axes(log_x_range, log_y_range, origin, width, height, x_label=None, y_label=None, tick_font=FONT_TICK, label_font=FONT_AXIS, label_every=(1, 1), buff=0.15)`: Log-log axes in decades, with 10^n tick labels, as (axes, frame).
- `plot_point(axes, log_x, log_y)`: The scene point of (log10 x, log10 y) on ``axes`` from log_axes.
- `curve_points(axes, x, y)`: Scene points of a curve given as linear (x, y) arrays, for set_points_as_corners.
- `dot_points(axes, xs, ys)`: Every dot's circle, end to end, in the order the dots arrive.
- `dot_cloud(points, per_dot, color, count, opacity)`: A series' dots as one VMobject, showing the first ``count`` of them as it runs.
- `static_cloud(points, color, opacity)`: Every dot of a series as one still VMobject.

- *phase, drawn as a clock hand*: `CLOCK_ATOM_RADIUS`, `CLOCK_HAND_COLOR`, `CLOCK_HAND_WIDTH`, `CLOCK_HAND_RATIO`, `CLOCK_DIAL_RADIUS`, `CLOCK_SWEEP_OPACITY`

### `interferometry.tools.clock`

`src/manim_atoms/interferometry/tools/clock.py` — Phase drawn as a clock hand: hands, dials, output ports and the phase budget.

- `clock_rate(interrogation_time)`: How fast a hand turns, fixed by how far it should get in one leg.
- `make_clock_hand(atom, phase)`: A hand riding an atom, pointing at the phase that arm has accumulated.
- `make_dial(center, caption=None, radius=CLOCK_DIAL_RADIUS)`: A clock face, for a phase that is too small to read off a moving atom.
- `dial_hand(center, phase, color, radius=CLOCK_DIAL_RADIUS)`: The same phase a clock hand shows, at a size you can actually read.
- `phase_sweep(center, phase_a, phase_b, radius=CLOCK_DIAL_RADIUS)`: The angle between two arms' hands: what the interferometer reads out.
- `ground_share(phase_a, phase_b)`: The share of the atoms the last pulse leaves in |g, p>.
- `ring_around(term, color)`: An ellipse drawn round one term of an equation.
- `budget_equation(lhs, term_prefix='', font_size=FONT_STATE)`: The budget with `lhs` on the left, as one expression.
- `leg_slope(start, end)`: How steeply a leg climbs: the rise per unit time from `start` to `end`.
- `draw_ports(scene, origin, length, p_ground, slope=CP_SLOPE, labels=True, extra=())`: The two output states the last pulse leaves the atoms in.
- `port_parts(scene, origin, length, p_ground, slope=CP_SLOPE)`: The pieces draw_ports is made of: empty guides, legs to fly, labels.
- `live_ports(scene, drawn, origin, length, share, slope=CP_SLOPE)`: Keep ports draw_ports has already flown in step with the phase.
- `fly_ports(scene, ports, length, labels=True, extra=())`: draw_ports for a continuous scene: every port in one beat, clock running.
- `readout_equation(center=CP_READOUT)`: What the angle on the dial becomes once the last pulse has fired.
- `show_phase_budget(scene, center, laser_struck, laser_label, difference_lhs=None, max_width=None, eq=None, label_side=DOWN)`: Phi split into its two terms, each marked with what it is worth.
- `along_port(origin, rise, x)`: Where a port leaving `origin` at slope `rise` is at time x.

### `interferometry.tools.gradiometer`

`src/manim_atoms/interferometry/tools/gradiometer.py` — The atom gradiometer: two clock interferometers on one baseline, one laser.

- `vertices(z0, lag)`: The four corners of one interferometer in the (time, baseline) plane.
- `gradiometer_frame(scene, title_tex)`: The furniture every gradiometer scene shares, played onto the screen.
- `laser_jumps(v)`: The laser's phase on each of a cloud's two hands, as (lab time, delta).

### `interferometry.tools.lmt`

`src/manim_atoms/interferometry/tools/lmt.py` — Large momentum transfer: sequences of single-photon pulses, each driving every arm it crosses (after Rudolph et al., PRL 124, 083604 (2020), Fig. 1c).

- `lmz_pulses(n, step, T, t0=0.0, stage=0)`: The LMT Mach-Zehnder of order n (odd), as Pulse objects for run_sequence: a pi/2 and (n - 1)/2 pulses out, a mirror of n pulses, (n - 1)/2 pulses back and a pi/2. Every pulse drives both arms, from whichever side opens (or, at the mirror and after it, closes) the gap by 2 hbar k; the sequence is symmetric in time about the middle of the mirror, so the arms close. Stages ``stage`` to ``stage + 2``: beam splitter, mirror, beam splitter.
- `lmt_ladder_pulses(kicks=LMT_KICKS, step=LMT_STEP, t0=LMT_T0)`: A pi/2 that splits the atom, then pi pulses alternating from below and above: each drives both arms, which reach it in opposite states, so one absorbs and the other is stimulated to emit and they are pushed apart by 2 hbar k a pulse.

### `interferometry.tools.phase_shear`

`src/manim_atoms/interferometry/tools/phase_shear.py` — Phase-shear readout: a tilted last pulse, and the fringes it writes on a cloud.

- `shear_phase(x, theta, phi, spacing)`: phi(x) = Phi + k theta x, with the drawn wavefront ``spacing`` as the wavelength -- so on screen the fringe period is spacing / sin(theta), exactly how far apart the tilted wavefronts cross the cloud.
- `excited_fraction(phase, contrast=SHEAR_CONTRAST)`: P_e = (1 - C cos phi) / 2, the excited port's share at phase phi.
- `phase_reading(fn)`: Something make_clock_hand can read a phase from: an object with a get_value(), here worked out afresh each frame by ``fn``.
- `make_beam(center, width, below, above, spacing)`: The last pulse as a beam rising to ``center``: a band ``width`` wide, from ``below`` under the centre to ``above`` over it, with a wavefront every ``spacing`` counted from the one through the centre, and a dashed axis. Built upright; rotate it about ``center`` to tilt it.
- class `PortImage(ImageMobject)`: A camera image of one output port: a Gaussian cloud, lit in the port's colour by the share of the atoms that came out there.
  - `.paint(share)`

### `interferometry.tools.pulse_sequence`

`src/manim_atoms/interferometry/tools/pulse_sequence.py` — Stepping an atom through any sequence of laser pulses, and playing it.

- class `Pulse()`: One laser pulse: when it fires, its area in units of pi (0.5 splits, 1 swaps), which side it comes from, which arms it drives (None: all), which arms leave the figure after it, and the stage it belongs to.
- class `Arm()`: One arm of the atom: its internal state ("g" or "e"), its velocity in recoils, and where it is in the free-falling frame (time, height).
- class `Step()`: What one pulse did. ``x`` is its lab time.
- class `Sequence()`: A run of the engine: one Step per pulse, every arm's corners (``paths``: name -> points, from where it was born to where it ended), the arms left after the last pulse (``ports``), and ``disp``.
- `run_sequence(pulses, start, u, v0=0.0, disp=no_displacement, until=None, port=SEQUENCE_PORT)`: Step one atom, in |g> at ``start`` (lab time, height) with velocity ``v0`` recoils, through ``pulses`` (in time order). After the last pulse the arms fly on to ``until`` (default: ``port`` past it): those legs are the output ports. ``disp(t)`` displaces everything (gravity: -g t^2 / 2 from the launch). Returns a Sequence.
- `play_sequence(scene, seq, atoms, *, span=None, ray_time=0.3, flash_time=0.35, fast_after=None, fast_pace=0.6, colors=None, before_pulse=None, with_pulse=None, after_step=None)`: Animate ``seq``: one ray per pulse, reaching from its side through to the furthest arm; a flash on every arm it kicks, recoloured to its new state; then the legs to the next pulse. ``atoms`` maps arm names to the atoms already on screen (``{"": atom}`` to start); the dict returned maps the arms left at the end.

### `interferometry.tools.pulses`

`src/manim_atoms/interferometry/tools/pulses.py` — Laser pulses on a space-time diagram: lab time across, height up.

- `photon_worldline(x_at_lower, z_from, z_to, slope=GR_SLOPE, z_at=GR_LOWER_Z)`: The segment of a pulse's worldline between two points on the baseline.
- `fire_pulse(scene, x_at_lower, flash, lag=GR_LAG, reference=False, note=None, z_near=GR_LOWER_Z, z_far=GR_UPPER_Z, quiet_x=None)`: Send one pulse up the baseline, reaching the far cloud `lag` later.
- `climbing_pulse(clock, x_at_lower, slope, z_from, z_to, z_at)`: A photon's worldline, drawn as far up the baseline as it has got.
- `sweep_pulse(scene, clock, x_at_lower, near, far, lag=GR_LAG, reference=False, note=None, z_near=GR_LOWER_Z, z_far=GR_UPPER_Z, quiet_x=None, fade=(), on_near=None, on_far=None)`: fire_pulse with lab time running: the pulse climbs, the atoms carry on.
- `launch_time(x_at_lower, z_at=GR_LOWER_Z)`: When a pulse that crosses height `z_at` at `x_at_lower` leaves the laser.
- `laser_caption(n, x_at_lower, z_at=GR_LOWER_Z)`: phi_n on the laser line, just right of where pulse n leaves it.
- `fire_vertical_pulse(scene, x, hits)`: One pulse climbing the diagram at time `x`, flashing what it crosses.
- `strobe_pulse(scene, clock, x, top, flash_at, on_arrival=None, hold=PULSE_HOLD)`: fire_vertical_pulse with lab time running.
- `kick_worldline(point, from_below, steepness=0.12, span=None)`: A photon's worldline arriving at `point` from below or from above: from the frame's edge, or from the (bottom, top) of `span`, to keep it out of a title or a caption row.
- `pulse_caption(tex, x)`: A pulse label on the caption row, offset clear of the beam it names.

### `interferometry.tools.squeezing`

`src/manim_atoms/interferometry/tools/squeezing.py` — Spin squeezing by a non-demolition measurement in an optical cavity.

- `cavity_atoms(center, radius, n=40, seed=4)`: The atoms in the cavity mode, each in the same superposition of |g> and |e>, so drawn halfway between the two states' colours.

### `interferometry.scenes.clock`

`src/manim_atoms/interferometry/scenes/clock.py` — The clock interferometer's phase, read out as the angle between two hands.

- Scene `ClockPhase(Scene)`: One interferometer -- one clock -- with the phase on show.
  - `.beat()`: The pause after each step: nothing here, a click on the slide version.
  - `.laser_jump(jumps)`: The laser writes its phase in: each (tracker, delta) hand turns by delta, on the spot, just after the pulse that wrote it.
  - `.pulse(x, n, hits)`: Pulse n, captioned with the laser phase phi_n it writes in.
  - `.phase_budget(budget)`: Hook: ClockPhaseTerms marks up what each term of the phase is worth.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/interferometry/scenes/clock.py ClockPhase`
- Scene `ClockPhaseTerms(ClockPhase)`: ClockPhase, and then what each term of the phase it read out is worth.
  - `.phase_budget(budget)`
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/interferometry/scenes/clock.py ClockPhaseTerms`

### `interferometry.scenes.gradiometer`

`src/manim_atoms/interferometry/scenes/gradiometer.py` — Two clock interferometers on one baseline, driven by one laser.

- Scene `GradiometerBase(Scene)`: The machinery every gradiometer scene shares: two clouds on one baseline, each split into two arms carrying a clock hand, each read out on its own dial and closed into a pair of ports.
  - `.beat()`: The pause after each step: nothing here, a click on the slide version.
  - `.vertices(cloud)`
  - `.nominal(cloud)`: Where on the baseline a cloud belongs.
  - `.displacement(cloud)`: How something passing through bows this cloud's worldline. Not at all, unless a subclass says so (GradiometerGWStretch's wave does).
  - `.open_arms(cloud)`: One cloud's seed becomes two arms, each carrying a hand.
  - `.port_extra()`: What rides along with the output ports. Nothing, unless lab time does.
  - `.port_slope(cloud)`: The slope a cloud's excited port leaves at: its kicked leg's.
  - `.close(sweeps)`: Read both dials, then let each pair of ports fly.
- class `RunsContinuously()`: Mixin: a gradiometer scene whose lab time never stops.
  - `.port_extra()`
  - `.close(sweeps)`: The sectors arrive while the ports fly, not before them.
  - `.open_arms(cloud)`
  - `.mirror(cloud)`: The pulse hands the excitation over, on the instant it arrives.
- Scene `Gradiometer(GradiometerBase)`: Two interferometers, one baseline, one laser -- so, two clocks.
  - `.pulse_note(k)`: Nothing: the pulses go uncaptioned (see construct).
  - `.laser_jump(k)`: Pulse k writes its phase onto both clouds' hands.
  - `.jump_steps(cloud)`: laser_jumps per hand, grouped by the pulse that makes them.
  - `.fly()`: Three pulses and two legs, one at a time.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/interferometry/scenes/gradiometer.py Gradiometer`
- Scene `GradiometerContinuous(RunsContinuously, Gradiometer)`: The same two clocks with lab time never stopped.
  - `.fly()`
  - `.shoot(k, near, far, fade=(), on_near=None, on_far=None, z_near=GR_LOWER_Z, z_far=GR_UPPER_Z)`: One pulse. No wave here, so every one of them is the quiet one.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/interferometry/scenes/gradiometer.py GradiometerContinuous`

### `trapping.physics.mot_loading`

`src/manim_atoms/trapping/physics/mot_loading.py` — The HiFAIS 3D MOT loading curves, as numbers.

- `load_loading_curves()`: {oven temperature / degC: {"t_ms", "n", "sem"} arrays}, coolest first.
- `load_loading_fits()`: {oven temperature / degC: {"rate", "loss", "onset_ms", "offset", "fit_max_ms", ...}}: the fitted model's parameters, coolest first.
- `loading_model(t_ms, fit)`: The fitted N(t): dN/dt = R - L N from N0 at the onset, N0 before it.

### `trapping.tools.cooling`

`src/manim_atoms/trapping/tools/cooling.py` — A magneto-optical trap drawn as a cartoon: its beams, coils and atom cloud.

- `project(v)`: A 3D direction (x right, y up, z out of the page) on the page.
- `oblique_ring(center, radius, color=GUIDE_COLOR)`: A circle in the plane across the push axis (y up, z out of the page), in the oblique view: the depth cue for beams that leave the page.
- `chevron(direction, tip, color, size=MOT_BEAM_WIDTH * 0.45)`: An open arrowhead: two strokes meeting at ``tip``, pointing along ``direction``.
- class `MotBeams(VGroup)`: Counter-propagating beam pairs crossing at ``center``, all one colour.
  - `.set_intensity(intensity)`
- `make_up_beam(color, center, reach=MOT_BEAM_REACH)`: The narrowband red MOT's seventh beam: from below only, holding the atoms up against gravity. Brighter than the MOT beams it rides inside, because it is the unbalanced one.
- class `Coils(VGroup)`: An anti-Helmholtz pair above and below the trap, with the current running opposite ways round them. How heavily they are drawn stands for the field gradient: ``set_gradient(COIL_STRONG_WIDTH)`` or ``COIL_WEAK_WIDTH``.
  - `.set_gradient(width)`
- `make_sawtooth(color, width=0.9, height=0.3, teeth=3)`: The shape of the red MOT's frequency modulation.
- class `SweepFan(VGroup)`: The 689 nm light swept in a sawtooth, drawn as a fan of arrows.
- class `AtomCloud(VGroup)`: A cloud of ``n`` atoms in a trap at ``center``.
- class `Oven(VGroup)`: A crucible with a nozzle on top, open at ``nozzle`` (the point the atoms come out of). Drawn warm inside, because it is hot.
- `make_push_beam(color, start, end)`: The push beam: narrow and bright like the up beam, running from ``start`` to ``end`` with its arrowheads pointing the way it pushes.
- `make_baffle(center, height=BAFFLE_HEIGHT, gap=BAFFLE_GAP)`: A wall across the beam line with a small hole in it at ``center``.
- class `AtomBeam(VGroup)`: A steady stream of atoms from ``start`` to ``end``, where they are caught: each fades out over the last ``fade`` of the way.

### `trapping.tools.dipole`

`src/manim_atoms/trapping/tools/dipole.py` — Two crossed dipole traps loaded from the red MOT, drawn as a cartoon.

- `make_mot_glow(center, radius, color=TRANSITION_689_COLOR)`: A MOT as a soft glow at ``center``, with a chevron at the end of each beam pointing in.
- `make_field_zero(y, x, color=lighten(GUIDE_COLOR))`: A pointer at the height of the quadrupole field's zero, from the side of the figure rather than on the traps, where it would hide the atoms.
- class `LoadingAtoms(VGroup)`: The red MOT's atoms, shared out between two dipole traps.
- class `SpinHistogram(VGroup)`: How the atoms are spread over m_F, pumped into +9/2 as ``pump`` goes 0 to 1.

### `trapping.tools.hifais`

`src/manim_atoms/trapping/tools/hifais.py` — The HiFAIS atom source drawn from its CAD, and its MOT loading curves.

- `chamber_view(path, height)`: One of the chamber renders (CHAMBER_TOP, CHAMBER_SIDE) as an image ``height`` tall.
- `chamber_label(text, target, direction, length=0.7)`: A label joined to ``target`` by a leader ``length`` long, leaving it in ``direction``. The text is outlined in the page colour, so it still reads where it overlaps the render.
- `at(image, px)`: A pixel of a render, on screen.
- `loading_axes(x_length, y_length)`: Axes, tick labels and axis labels, as (axes, frame), in ms and 1e9.
- `loading_cutoff(axes)`: The atom number the fits stop at, across the plot, labelled at its right end: above it the MOT goes unstable.
- `loading_points(axes, run, color)`: One run's points with their error bars.
- `loading_fit(axes, fit, color)`: The fitted model: solid over the points it was fitted to, dashed where it is carried on past them to the end of the run.
- `dimension(start, end, text, side)`: A dimension: a double arrow from ``start`` to ``end`` with its length beside the middle, on ``side``. Drawn in the photo-label yellow with a dark outline, since it lies across the render.
- `loading_rate_line(axes, fit, color, top=1.2)`: The initial slope, N0 + R (t - t0), from the onset up to ``top``: the loading rate the paper quotes, as a line on the plot.
- `temperature_key(temperatures)`: One swatch per oven temperature, in a row, headed "Oven".

### `trapping.tools.sequence`

`src/manim_atoms/trapping/tools/sequence.py` — One shot of the experiment: the stages, the Sr levels they drive, the timeline.

- `snapshot_index(t_ms)`: Which snapshot shows the cloud at ``t_ms``: the last one taken by then.
- `snapshot_ms(t_ms)`: When the snapshot showing the cloud at ``t_ms`` was taken.
- class `Stage()`: One stage of the sequence: its colour key, its label, and, where it has them, the transition it drives, the stretch of imaging video that shows it and the paper that covers it.
- class `Timeline(VGroup)`: A row of coloured blocks, one per stage, with the label under each.
  - `.activate(i)`
- class `References(VGroup)`: A brace under each run of stages a paper covers, numbered, and the numbered list of papers below. The one covering the running stage is lit.
  - `.cite(n)`: Animations lighting reference ``n`` (None for none) and dimming the rest.
- `stage_heading(stage)`: The running stage's name, and the transition it drives, in big type.
- `caption(text, heading)`: A grey caption under ``heading``, left-aligned with it.

### `trapping.tools.slicing`

`src/manim_atoms/trapping/tools/slicing.py` — Velocity slicing: a long clock pulse picks the slowest atoms out of a cloud.

- `excitation(u)`: The pi pulse's excitation probability at Doppler detuning u (in Omega).
- `thermal(u, sigma=SLICE_THERMAL_SIGMA)`: The velocity distribution before the pulse, peak normalised to one.
- class `VelocityPlot(VGroup)`: The velocity distribution, stacked by internal state, with the pulse's excitation probability over it on the same scale.
  - `.c2p(u, y)`
- class `SlicingCloud(VGroup)`: ``excite`` and ``push`` as on VelocityPlot; the drift runs by itself.

### `trapping.scenes.cooling`

`src/manim_atoms/trapping/scenes/cooling.py` — Cooling Sr: the three MOT stages that open every shot, as a cartoon.

- `temperature_tag(key)`: The cloud's temperature at stage ``key``, as MathTex in its corner.
- `gradient_tag(key, coils)`: The field gradient, beside the upper coil it is drawn with.
- `duration_tag(key, block)`: How long a stage runs, over its block of the timeline.
- Scene `CoolingSequence(MovingCameraScene)`: The blue MOT, the modulated red MOT and the narrowband red MOT: the light, the field gradient and the cloud at each, with the Sr levels and the timeline beside them. One stage_break() per stage.
  - `.stage_break()`: The pause after each stage. A slide wrapper stops here instead.
  - `.upstream(levels)`: The oven filling the 2D MOT, then the push beam switching on and the stream setting off for the 3D MOT; returns that stream.
  - `.heading(i)`: Stage ``i``'s heading, in the upper left; the modulated red MOT's carries the depth of its sweep under the transition it drives.
  - `.next_stage(timeline, i, heading, anims)`: Move the timeline and heading on to stage ``i``, alongside ``anims``, and put up its duration; returns the new heading.
  - `.cool(cloud, key, tag, *anims, run_time)`: Shrink and cool the cloud to where stage ``key`` leaves it, the temperature tag changing over halfway; returns the new tag.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/trapping/scenes/cooling.py CoolingSequence`

### `trapping.scenes.dipole`

`src/manim_atoms/trapping/scenes/dipole.py` — Loading the two dipole traps from the red MOT, then spin-polarising them.

- Scene `DipoleTrapLoading(Scene)`: The red MOT shared out into two crossed dipole traps, then the atoms spin-polarised into m_F = +9/2, with the levels and the timeline beside them. One stage_break() per stage.
  - `.stage_break()`: The pause after each stage. A slide wrapper stops here instead.

  - `.next_stage(timeline, i, heading, step, text)`: Move the timeline, heading and caption on to stage ``i`` of this scene's three; returns the new heading and caption.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/trapping/scenes/dipole.py DipoleTrapLoading`

### `trapping.scenes.hifais`

`src/manim_atoms/trapping/scenes/hifais.py` — HiFAIS: a high-flux source of cold strontium, and the MOT it loads.

- `frame_caption()`: The support frame's size, W x D x H in mm, as a caption under the two views.
- Scene `HighFluxLoading(Scene)`: The HiFAIS chamber from above and from the side, labelled, then its MOT loading curves at each oven temperature with their fits.
  - `.beat()`: The pause after each step: nothing here, a click on the slide version.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/trapping/scenes/hifais.py HighFluxLoading`

### `trapping.scenes.sequence`

`src/manim_atoms/trapping/scenes/sequence.py` — One shot of the experiment, stage by stage, beside the imaging of it.

- Scene `ExperimentSequence(Scene)`: One shot, stage by stage: the timeline, the Sr levels each stage drives, the papers that cover them, and the imaging video of the cloud run on the same clock.

### `trapping.scenes.slicing`

`src/manim_atoms/trapping/scenes/slicing.py` — Velocity slicing: the clock pulse that picks out the slowest atoms.

- `readout(when, values, color, plot)`: 'Before slicing T ~ ... pi-pulse fidelity ~ ...', over the plot's left end.

## tweezers

### `tweezers.physics.rearrangement`

`src/manim_atoms/tweezers/physics/rearrangement.py` — A tweezer array's numbers: its sites, which of them load, and the moves that rearrange the loaded ones into a defect-free block.

- class `Plan()`: A rearrangement: the traps kept, where each starts and ends, and the loaded traps dropped as surplus. ``kept`` and ``dropped`` index the sites; ``start`` and ``end`` are (len(kept), 2), in ``kept``'s order.
- `square_sites(rows, cols, pitch)`: The (rows * cols, 2) positions of a square lattice of traps ``pitch`` apart, centred on the origin, row by row from the top left.
- `load_sites(n, fill, rng)`: Which of n traps caught an atom, each with probability ``fill``. ``rng`` is a numpy Generator, seeded so a scene loads the same way every render.
- `plan_rearrangement(sites, loaded, targets)`: Pair loaded traps with target sites so the summed squared distance is least, and drop the loaded traps left over.
- `positions(plan, share)`: Every kept trap ``share`` of the way from its start to its end.
- `longest_move(plan)`: The farthest any kept trap travels: what sets how long the move takes.

## aion

### `aion.style`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/style.py` — The AION scenes' style: the interferometry and trapping styles (AION draws on both) plus AION's own palettes: the long-baseline cartoon, the spacetime sheet and gravitational waves, the dark-matter field and the solar system, the light-shift beam, LIGO's arms, the data plots (the DAI fringes, the GW and ULDM sensitivity curves) and the km-scale table.

- *a long-baseline detector*: `SHAFT_COLOR`, `SHAFT_WALL_WIDTH`, `SOURCE_STROKE_WIDTH`, `BASELINE_BEAM_OPACITY`, `LAUNCH_STROKE_WIDTH`, `FONT_SOURCE`
- *spacetime and gravitational waves*: `SHEET_COLOR`, `CREST_COLOR`, `TROUGH_COLOR`, `HORIZON_COLOR`, `HORIZON_GLOW`, `SHEET_STROKE_WIDTH`, `HORIZON_MESH_WIDTH`, `HORIZON_MESH_OPACITY`, `BURST_STROKE_WIDTH`, `STRAIN_COLOR`, `STRAIN_STROKE_WIDTH`
- *an oscillating background field*: `FIELD_COLOR`, `FIELD_STROKE_WIDTH`, `EARTH_COLOR`, `MOON_COLOR`, `SUN_COLOR`, `BODY_OPACITY`, `BODY_MIN_RADIUS`
- *an injected light shift*: `LIGHT_SHIFT_COLOR`, `LIGHT_SHIFT_STYLE`
- *energy levels*: `LEVEL_RESONANCE_STYLE`
- *an optical Michelson interferometer*: `X_ARM_COLOR`, `Y_ARM_COLOR`, `OUTPUT_COLOR`, `BEAM_STROKE_WIDTH`, `BEAM_GLOW_WIDTH`, `BEAM_GLOW_OPACITY`
- *data plots (matplotlib)*: `LOWER_CLOUD_COLOR`, `UPPER_CLOUD_COLOR`, `LLN_COLOR`, `SQL_COLOR`, `LOWER_PULSE_MARK_COLOR`, `UPPER_PULSE_MARK_COLOR`, `HLN_COLOR`, `SQL_BAND_OPACITIES`, `IMPRINTED_SIGNAL_COLOR`, `RECOVERED_SIGNAL_COLOR`, `FRINGE_DOT_OPACITY`, `FRINGE_DIM_OPACITY`, `NEWEST_RING_RADIUS`, `NEWEST_RING_WIDTH`, `GW_DETECTOR_COLORS`, `GW_REGION_OPACITY`, `GW_MERGER_NEAR_COLOR`, `GW_MERGER_FAR_COLOR`, `GW_MERGER_Z_RANGE`, `GW_MERGER_TIME_COLORS`, `GW_BAND_EDGE_STYLE`, `GW_TRACK_WIDTH`, `GW_TRACK_AHEAD_OPACITY`, `GW_SOURCE_COLOR`, `GW_SOURCE_RADIUS`, `GW_SOURCE_GLOW_RADIUS`, `GW_SOURCE_GLOW_OPACITY`, `GW_DATA_WINDOW_COLOR`, `GW_TRACK_CROWD_WIDTH`, `ULDM_COLORS`, `ULDM_CURVE_WIDTH`, `ULDM_EXCLUDED_STYLE`, `ULDM_EXCLUDED_EDGE`, `ULDM_MARK_STYLE`, `ULDM_MARK_FAINT_OPACITY`, `ULDM_MARK_DOT_RADIUS`, `ULDM_LABEL_OUTLINE`, `FONT_INSET_TICK`, `FONT_INSET_LABEL`
- *km-scale challenges table*: `FONT_TABLE_HEADING`, `FONT_TABLE_NAME`, `FONT_TABLE_NOTE`, `FONT_TABLE_CELL`, `TABLE_RULE_STYLE`
- `merger_color(z)`: A merger track's shade: GW_MERGER_NEAR_COLOR at the low end of GW_MERGER_Z_RANGE fading to GW_MERGER_FAR_COLOR at the high end, in log z.

### `aion.physics.gw_signals`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/physics/gw_signals.py` — Gravitational-wave signals and detector sensitivities, as numbers.

- `mass_tex(M)`: A total mass as TeX math (no $), e.g. 60\,M_\odot or 10^{4}\,M_\odot.
- `load_sensitivity(stem, smooth=True)`: (f, h_c) arrays from manim_atoms/data/gw_sensitivity/<stem>.csv, smoothed as SMOOTHING says unless smooth=False.
- `smooth_log_log(f, h, start, sigma, ramp=0.15, step=0.01)`: A curve blurred by a Gaussian of width sigma dex in log f, log h.
- `luminosity_distance(z)`: Luminosity distance in light-seconds, flat LambdaCDM.
- `symmetric_mass_ratio(q)`: eta = m1 m2 / (m1 + m2)^2 for a mass ratio q = m2 / m1.
- `phenom_a_frequencies(M, z, q=1)`: PhenomA merger, ringdown, ringdown-width and cutoff frequencies / Hz, in the detector frame (redshifted mass).
- `merger_strain(f, M, z, q=1)`: Characteristic strain 2 f |h(f)|; NaN above the ringdown cutoff.
- `frequency_before_merger(t, M, z, q=1)`: GW frequency / Hz a time t / s before merger (leading-order chirp, redshifted chirp mass).
- `time_before_merger(f, M, z, q=1)`: Inverse of frequency_before_merger: seconds left at frequency f.
- `merger_track(M, z, q=1, t_start=TRACK_START, n=600)`: (f, h_c) of a merger from t_start before it to the ringdown cutoff.

### `aion.physics.km_scale`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/physics/km_scale.py` — What going from the tabletop prototype to AION-km asks for, in numbers.

- `waist_for_rayleigh_range(z_r, wavelength=CLOCK_WAVELENGTH)`: The Gaussian waist w0 whose Rayleigh range pi w0^2 / lambda is z_r: the narrowest beam that stays collimated (radius within sqrt 2) that far.
- `power_for_same_rabi(waist)`: The power a beam of this waist needs to drive the prototype's pi pulse in the same time: Rabi frequency goes as sqrt(peak intensity), and peak intensity as P / w^2, so P scales as w^2.
- `pulse_count(n=KM_LMT, q=1)`: Pulses in an n-fold LMT sequence with Q mirror stages: 2 Q (2n - 1) + 1, AION 2020 below its eq. (2.5).
- `fidelity_for_contrast(pulses, contrast=np.exp(-1))`: The per-pulse transfer efficiency f with f^pulses = contrast: what each pulse must reach for that much of the atoms to make it through.

### `aion.physics.uldm_sensitivity`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/physics/uldm_sensitivity.py` — AION's reach for ultralight scalar dark matter coupled to photons, as numbers.

- `model_reach(m, L, T, dphi, n)`: |d_e| reached at SNR 1 by a gradiometer (L, T, dphi, n), eqs. 3.5-3.7.
- `load_uldm_sensitivity(stem, extend=True)`: (m_phi / eV, |d_e|) arrays from manim_atoms/data/uldm_sensitivity/<stem>.csv.
- `mass_from_frequency(f)`: m_phi / eV of a field oscillating at f / Hz.
- `frequency_from_mass(m)`: f / Hz of a field of mass m / eV.
- `coupling_at(stem, mass)`: |d_e| on a curve at `mass` / eV, linear in log-log; nan off its ends.

### `aion.tools.baseline`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/tools/baseline.py` — A long-baseline atom gradiometer in cartoon, for a static slide.

- `launch_loop(cloud_center, height=BL_LAUNCH_HEIGHT, width=BL_LAUNCH_WIDTH, color=ATOM_COLOR)`: Up from the cloud, over the top and back down: the fountain launch, with an arrowhead on the way down.
- `source(port, label='Sr')`: An atom source on the shaft's left: a box, a transfer tube from it to ``port`` on the wall, and its atoms' path along the tube.
- `make_baseline(bottom, top, n=4, label='1\\,\\mathrm{km}', x=0.0)`: The shaft from ``bottom`` to ``top`` (heights), centred on ``x``, with ``n`` interferometers evenly along it and the baseline arrow labelled ``label``. Returns a VGroup; its parts are named attributes too.

### `aion.tools.gradiometer_gw`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/tools/gradiometer_gw.py` — A gravitational wave passing through the gradiometer.

- `strain(t)`: h(t) at the detector, normalised to +-1, at GW_THETA at the first pulse.
- `gw_lag(t, gain=GW_LAG_GAIN)`: Light travel time across the baseline while the wave is passing.
- `gw_arrival_lags(z)`: How late each pulse reaches the point z on the baseline once the wave is passing.
- `quiet_arrival(k)`: When pulse k would have reached the lower cloud with no wave passing.
- `gw_displacement(t, z0)`: How far the wave has moved a cloud nominally at z0 on the baseline.
- `trace_point(t)`: Where lab time t sits on the strain trace.
- `make_strain_trace(label='h(t)')`: The wave above the diagram, on the diagram's own time axis.
- `arrival_dots(near_times, far_times)`: A pair of markers per pulse on the trace, where it reaches the near cloud and where it reaches the far, as the dark-matter gradiometer marks its field: each in its cloud's mark colour, near then far for each pulse. The gap in each pair is the light travel time the wave is changing.
- `strain_marker(clock)`: field_marker's twin: where on the wave the diagram has got to.
- `gw_vertices(z0, lags)`: The four corners when the three pulses arrive `lags` after they are fired.
- `arrival_note(point, lag)`: Names an arrival early or late against the quiet baseline's own L/c.

### `aion.tools.gw_plot`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/tools/gw_plot.py` — Log-log characteristic-strain plots in manim.

- `sensitivity_axes(log_f_range, log_h_range, origin, width, height, x_label='Frequency / Hz', y_label='Characteristic strain', **kwargs)`: log_axes labelled for characteristic strain against frequency.
- `detector_region(axes, stem, color)`: A detector's curve, and its region shaded up to the top of the axes.

### `aion.tools.ligo`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/tools/ligo.py` — LIGO's Michelson interferometer, drawn to be lit by a passing wave.

- `strain(t)`: h(t), normalised to a peak of 1: a few cycles under a smooth envelope.
- class `Panel()`: Where the drawing goes: shrunk by `scale` about the origin (strokes too), then moved by `shift`. The default leaves it filling the frame.
  - `.at(scale, source, target)`: The panel of `scale` that puts the drawing's point `source` on `target`.
  - `.point(p)`
  - `.redraw(draw)`: always_redraw, with each redrawn mobject placed.
- `phase_difference(t, h=strain)`: phi_x - phi_y at the detector: 2k (L_x - L_y), which is linear in h.
- `mirror_positions(t, h=strain)`: Plus polarisation: the x arm stretches exactly as the y arm squeezes.
- `wave(start, end, amplitude, phase, frac=1.0, k=K_LIGHT)`: A sine riding the segment start -> end, drawn out to `frac` of its length.
- `beam(start, end, frac=1.0, opacity=1.0)`: The faint band a beam's wave rides on.
- `make_mirror(vertical)`: A test mass: a thin slab, upright if ``vertical``, else lying flat.
- `make_splitter()`: A half-silvered plate at 45 degrees: it reflects light from the laser up the y arm, and light coming back down the x arm into the detector.
- `make_laser()`: The laser: a box at LASER, labelled under it.
- `make_detector()`: A photodiode facing up the output port.
- `detector_glow(now, h=strain)`: Power at the detector, sin^2(dphi / 2), drawn as light pooling on it.
- `make_strain_trace(now, h=strain, span=TRACE_T, panel=FULL_FRAME, amplitude=TRACE_AMPLITUDE)`: h(t) drawn out as it arrives, with a dot on the present; the panel spans the stretch `span` of lab time. `amplitude` is the peak's height before the panel scales it.
- `returning_waves(now, h=strain, panel=FULL_FRAME)`: The light back from each arm, overlaid where the two recombine.
- `run(scene, now, to, *anims)`: Advance the lab clock to `to`, playing `anims` over the same stretch.
- `make_apparatus(now, h=strain, panel=FULL_FRAME)`: The title, the optics and their labels, with the test masses riding the wave. Returns (the title and labels, the optics, which go over the light, the arm labels).
- `make_light(now, lit_in, lit_arm, h=strain, panel=FULL_FRAME)`: The beams, chained so their phase runs on from one to the next, and the glow on the detector. `lit_in` and `lit_arm` say how far the light has got down the input beam and the arms.
- `make_equation(panel=FULL_FRAME)`: Delta phi in the arm lengths, then in h, under the readout panel; and the scale of the real thing under that.

### `aion.tools.uldm`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/tools/uldm.py` — An oscillating ultralight dark-matter field, and the clock transition it moves.

- `dm_field(t, t0=CP_T0)`: The field's modulation of omega_A at time t, normalised to +-1.
- `dm_phase(rate, t_from, t_to, t0=CP_T0)`: What an arm's hand winds up while excited from t_from to t_to.
- `make_field_trace(windows, z=DM_TRACE_Z, amplitude=DM_TRACE_AMPLITUDE, x_range=DM_TRACE_X, t0=CP_T0, pulses=None)`: The driving field along the top of the diagram, on its own time axis.
- `field_marker(now, z=DM_TRACE_Z, amplitude=DM_TRACE_AMPLITUDE, x_range=DM_TRACE_X, t0=CP_T0)`: A dot riding the trace at the instant the level diagram is showing.
- `dm_upper(now, center=DM_LEVELS, scale=1.0)`: Where |e> sits at time `now`, with the field dragging omega_A around.
- `make_modulated_levels(now, center=DM_LEVELS, scale=1.0, text_scale=1.0)`: The clock transition with omega_A modulated, against a fixed laser.

### `aion.tools.uldm_plot`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/tools/uldm_plot.py` — AION's reach for ultralight dark matter, as a small log-log inset.

- `clipped(stem, top, x_range=None)`: A curve's (log m, log d), cut to the stretch under `top` around its lowest point: where it comes down through `top` on the left, if it does (the AION curves carried below 0.3 Hz do), and goes up through it on the right -- and, given `x_range` (log m), to the axes' left and right edges too, which the AION curves carried below 0.3 Hz run past.
- `log_x_range(axes)`: The axes' mass range, (log m) at their left and right edges.
- `uldm_axes(origin, width, height)`: The inset's frame: decades of m_phi / eV and |d_e|, as (axes, frame).
- `excluded_region(axes)`: The grey region already ruled out, and the line along its lower edge.
- `uldm_curves(axes, stems=tuple(ULDM_SCENARIOS))`: Each stage's reach, stem: line, clipped to the frame of the axes.
- `uldm_labels(axes)`: Each AION stage's name beside its curve, in its colour, outlined against the plot.
- `excluded_label(axes, font_size=FONT_INSET_TICK, at=ULDM_EXCLUDED_LABEL, side=ORIGIN)`: The grey region named, hung off `at` (log m, log d_e) on `side`.
- `uldm_inset(origin, width, height)`: The whole inset, its axes' lower-left corner at `origin`.
- `reach(stem, mass)`: log10 |d_e| on a stage's curve at `mass`, or None off its ends.
- `deepest_reach(mass, stems=ULDM_INSET_STEMS)`: (stem, log10 |d_e|) of the curve reaching the smallest coupling at `mass`, or (None, None) where no curve covers it.
- `mass_mark(axes, mass, on=None, label='m_\\phi')`: A mass marked across the inset.
- `mass_label(axes, mass, label='m_\\phi')`: `label` at the foot of the mark: right of the line, where the plot is emptiest at every mass, unless the right-hand edge is too close.

### `aion.plots.dai_fringes`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/plots/dai_fringes.py` — Excitation-fraction fringes, the Lissajous ellipse and the imprinted-signal scans from the AION DAI data.

- `deck_fonts()`: A context to build and save the figures in: tick labels are made when a figure is drawn, so the fonts have to hold until it is saved.
- `hexed(color)`: A matplotlib colour from a manim one (or a hex string, passed through).
- `load(run)`: One run's CSV from data/dai_fringes/ as {column: array}, comment lines skipped.
- `load_adev()`: The Allan deviation CSV, as load() returns it.
- `load_sigma()`: {label: (sigma, error)} in urad for the Allan deviation's inset: "HLN", "LLN" and "SQL".
- `load_signals()`: {injected Hz: {"fit" | "true": (f_hz, value)}}, in frequency order.
- `dark_axes(ax)`: Style matplotlib axes for the dark slide background: no top or right spine, foreground-coloured ticks and labels.
- `legend(ax, markerscale=3, **kwargs)`: A frameless legend in the slide's foreground, its scatter keys made solid.
- `fringes_figure(lln, hln)`: Excitation against laser phase step for both interferometers, the quiet run (``lln``) above the noisy one (``hln``).
- `lissajous_figure(runs)`: Upper against lower excitation; runs is a list of (data, color, label).
- `adev_inset(ax, sigma, runs)`: sigma_<dphi> of each run in ``runs`` beside the SQL's, as the paper's inset.
- `adev_figure(adev, runs, sigma=None)`: Allan deviation against averaging time; runs is a list of (key, color, label).
- `frequency_unit(hz)`: (scale, unit) to show frequencies near hz in: uHz below half a mHz.
- `signals_figure(runs)`: One panel per injected frequency, from load_signals().

### `aion.plots.gw_sensitivity`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/plots/gw_sensitivity.py` — Characteristic-strain sensitivity curves of LISA, LIGO, ET, AION-10, AION-100, AION-km and AEDGE, with black-hole merger tracks laid over them.

- `draw_merger(ax, M, z, q=1, label_mass=False)`: Draw one merger track, dotted at the TIME_MARKERS it spans.
- `merger_legends(ax, redshifts)`: Two legends, lower left: one track per redshift, and one dot per time-to-merger marker.
- `dark_axes(ax)`: Style matplotlib axes for the dark slide background: no top or right spine, foreground-coloured ticks and labels.
- `sensitivity_figure()`: The whole figure: every detector's curve and region, and the merger tracks.

### `aion.scenes.aedge`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/aedge.py` — AEDGE: the same instrument in space, on both of the talk's plots at once.

- `uldm_stage(axes, curves, name)`: (curves, label) for one stage of the dark-matter panel.

### `aion.scenes.dai_data`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/dai_data.py` — The AION DAI data built up shot by shot.

- `load(run)`: One run's first N_SHOTS shots as {column: array}, sorted by laser phase step.
- `plot_axes(x_range, x_length, y_length, x_ticks, x_label, y_label)`: Axes, tick labels and axis labels, as (axes, frame).
- `fringe_plot(y_length, origin, x_label=True)`: The fringe panel's (axes, frame): excitation against phase step over 0 to 2 pi, its origin at ``origin``.

- Scene `FringesFirst(FringesToEllipse)`: FringesToEllipse starting from the finished fringes, dimmed, lighting each shot as it lands on the ellipse.
  - settings: `FRINGES_FIRST`
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/dai_data.py FringesFirst`
- Scene `FringesFirstNoisy(Noisy, FringesFirst)`: FringesFirst on the noisy run.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/dai_data.py FringesFirstNoisy`
- Scene `LaserNoiseLissajous(Scene)`: The quiet run in full, then shrunk to a top panel while the noisy run's shots land on the same Lissajous ellipse.
  - `.beat()`: The pause after each step: nothing here, a click on the slide version.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/dai_data.py LaserNoiseLissajous`

### `aion.scenes.gradiometer_gw`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/gradiometer_gw.py` — A gravitational wave passing through the gradiometer.

- Scene `GradiometerGW(GradiometerBase)`: A wave modulates the light travel time, so the pulses arrive early or late.
  - settings: `REFERENCE`
  - `.rest(cloud)`: Where the cloud is when lab time starts.
  - `.crossing(cloud, k)`: Where the cloud is when pulse k reaches it.
  - `.dot_times()`: The lab time each trace marker stands for, in self.dots' order: here one per pulse, at its firing.
  - `.pulse_dots(k)`: The trace markers that belong to pulse k.
  - `.pulse_note(k)`: What pulse k is captioned with, if anything.
  - `.fly()`: Three pulses and two legs, one at a time.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/gradiometer_gw.py GradiometerGW`
- class `WaveRunsContinuously(RunsContinuously)`: RunsContinuously for the scenes with a wave passing through: lab time starts as the first pulse leaves the laser, the strain trace's marker rides on it, and every pulse is fired where the wave has it arriving.
  - `.fly()`
  - `.shoot(k, near, far, fade=(), on_near=None, on_far=None)`: One pulse, fired the way this scene's geometry has it arriving.
- Scene `GradiometerGWContinuous(WaveRunsContinuously, GradiometerGW)`: GradiometerGW with the pulses climbing while the atoms fly.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/gradiometer_gw.py GradiometerGWContinuous`
- Scene `GradiometerGWStretch(GradiometerGW)`: The same wave drawn as a stretching baseline, for comparison.
  - settings: `REFERENCE`
  - `.displacement(cloud)`
  - `.crossing(cloud, k)`
  - `.pulse_note(k)`: The bow is the claim here, so it is named once and not again.
  - `.dot_times()`
  - `.pulse_dots(k)`
  - `.port_slope(cloud)`: The kicked leg's slope with the bow taken back out.
  - `.fly()`: Three pulses and two legs, one at a time, on bowed worldlines.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/gradiometer_gw.py GradiometerGWStretch`
- Scene `GradiometerGWStretchContinuous(WaveRunsContinuously, GradiometerGWStretch)`: GradiometerGWStretch with the pulses climbing while the atoms fly.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/gradiometer_gw.py GradiometerGWStretchContinuous`

### `aion.scenes.gravitational_waves`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/gravitational_waves.py` — Gravitational waves from a binary black hole merger.

- `separation(t)`: Orbital separation (half the distance between the holes) at time t.
- `omega(t)`: Orbital angular frequency at time t, frozen at both ends.
- `orbital_phase(t)`: Accumulated orbital phase, zero at t = 0.
- `hole_positions(t)`: Centres of the two holes, diametrically opposite on the orbit.
- `smooth_step(x)`: The cubic smoothstep, 0 below 0 and 1 above 1, with zero slope at both ends.
- `strain(t_emit)`: Wave amplitude emitted at time t_emit: switches on, chirps, rings down.
- `wells(x, y, t, gain=1.0)`: The static dent each hole makes, blended into one well at the merger.
- `sheet_height(x, y, t, gain=1.0)`: Height of the spacetime sheet at (x, y) and scene time t.
- `height_colors(z)`: Map an array of heights onto the trough-sheet-crest ramp.
- class `SheetLine(VMobject)`: A grid line that sits at the back of the camera's depth sort.
  - `.get_gradient_start_and_end_points()`
- `make_sheet()`: The wireframe sheet, flat, with each line's sampling stashed on it.
- `refresh_sheet(grid, t, gain=1.0)`: Re-evaluate every grid line at time t and recolour it by height.
- `make_black_hole(radius=BH_RADIUS)`: A black sphere with a warm rim mesh.
- `follow_orbit(hole, clock, which, gain, radius=BH_RADIUS)`: Keep a hole on its orbit and resting in the bottom of its own well.
- `observed_strain(t)`: h(t) for an observer far out along +x, in the sheet's own height units.
- `make_trace(clock, center=TRACE_CENTER, width=TRACE_WIDTH)`: A polyline of h(t) up to the current clock, pinned to the bottom edge.
- Scene `BlackHoleMerger(ThreeDScene)`: Two black holes spiral in, radiating, and merge into one ringing remnant.
  - settings: `CAMERA`, `AMBIENT_ROTATION`, `TITLE`
  - `.entrance(clock)`: Animations to play as the sheet and the title come in.
  - `.show_signal(clock)`: Bring in whatever reads the waves off the sheet, driven by clock.
  - `.after_ringdown(spacetime)`: Anything to do once the sheet has settled; spacetime is the sheet and the remnant, updaters already stopped on the sheet.
  - `.beat()`: The pause once the signal is up and once the ringdown has settled (after the settling, so a click never lands on a still sheet): nothing here, a click on the slide version.
  - `.merge(sheet, clock, gain)`: Stages 2-5 on a live, flat sheet with the clock at zero: two holes dent it, spiral in and merge, and the remnant rings down. Ends held on the settled sheet, still live; returns the remnant.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/gravitational_waves.py BlackHoleMerger`
- `ligo_strain(t)`: The merger's h at clock time t, normalised to a peak of 1.
- `side_frame_center(camera, zoom, screen_x)`: The frame_center that puts the sheet's centre at screen_x.
- `source_frequency(t)`: (f / Hz, real seconds left) of the source at scene time t: the chirp up to the merger frequency over the inspiral, then on through the ringdown to the track's cutoff while the holes merge.
- class `SideCamera(ThreeDCamera)`: A ThreeDCamera whose frame-fixed mobjects ignore frame_center.
  - `.transform_points_pre_display(mobject, points)`
- Scene `MergerOnSensitivityPlot(BlackHoleMerger)`: The merger on the left; on the right, its signal crossing LIGO's band.
  - settings: `WITH_LIGO`, `CAMERA`, `AMBIENT_ROTATION`
  - `.merge(sheet, clock, gain)`: Once beside LIGO, then, the sheet let go flat and the clock wound back, again beside the plot.
  - `.show_signal(clock)`
  - `.entrance(clock)`: LIGO on the right, lit, standing still until the clock runs; or, without it, the plot, up from the start with the source waiting at the low end of its track.
  - `.show_ligo(clock)`: The chirp strip under the sheet; LIGO is already up.
  - `.show_plot(clock)`
  - `.plot_entrance(clock)`: The sensitivity plot and the chirp strip, added fixed in frame; returns the animations that fade them in.
  - `.after_ringdown(spacetime)`
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/gravitational_waves.py MergerOnSensitivityPlot`

### `aion.scenes.light_shift`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/light_shift.py` — A light shift injected into one interferometer of the gradiometer.

- Scene `DarkMatterPhaseContinuous(DarkMatterPhase)`: The same figure with lab time never stopped.
  - `.port_extra()`
  - `.close(dial, sweep, gap, c)`: All at once here, because the ports are still the atoms flying.
  - `.fly()`
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/uldm.py DarkMatterPhaseContinuous`
- Scene `DarkMatterGradiometer(RunsContinuously, GradiometerBase)`: The field through the gradiometer: where the differential phase comes from.
  - `.pulse_note(k)`: The lag, named on the first pulse; the rest have nothing to add.
  - `.fly()`
  - `.shoot(k, near, far, fade=(), on_near=None, on_far=None, z_near=GR_LOWER_Z, z_far=GR_UPPER_Z)`: One pulse, at the quiet baseline's L/c: nothing here moves the light.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/uldm.py DarkMatterGradiometer`
- Scene `DarkMatterField(Scene)`: What an ultralight dark-matter field is, and why a clock can see it.
  - `.hold()`: Let the field run through one whole oscillation.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/uldm.py DarkMatterField`

### `aion.scenes.uldm_scale`

`src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/uldm_scale.py` — How big an ultralight dark-matter wave is, measured against the solar system.

- `compton(mass)`: lambda_C in metres for a mass in eV.
- Scene `DarkMatterScale(Scene)`: An ultralight dark-matter wave laid across the Earth, Moon and Sun.
  - `.hold()`: Let the wave run through one whole period.
  - `.screen_x(metres)`
  - `.body_labels(*named)`: A name under each body, at the current view: (name, x, radius).
  - `.wavelength_marks(mass, wavelength, frequency, note=None)`: One wavelength braced under the wave, and the numbers for this mass.
  - `.fly_to(view, mass, outgoing)`: Move the camera to `view`, with the wave out of sight while it goes.
  - `.reveal(labels, marks)`
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/uldm_scale.py DarkMatterScale`
- Scene `DarkMatterScalePlot(Scene)`: AION's reach in the photon coupling, full size, with three masses across its range marked and each labelled with the scale of its Compton wavelength: the plot of DarkMatterScale's inset, without the fly-out.
  - settings: `TITLE`
  - `.beat()`: A click on the slide version.
  - `uv run manim -ql src/manim_atoms/aion/scenes/uldm_scale.py DarkMatterScalePlot`

## slides

### `slides.cli`

`src/manim_atoms/slides/cli.py` — Render, present or convert a deck of manim-slides slides.

- `manim_slides(*args, **kwargs)`: Run manim-slides with this interpreter, so it sees the same packages.
- `render(deck, main, jobs, fps, args)`: Render ``deck``'s slides (``args``: [l|m|h] [Slide ...]), ``jobs`` at a time.
- `main(argv=None)`: The manim-atoms-deck command: render, present, html or player.

### `slides.deck`

`src/manim_atoms/slides/deck.py` — Any manim_atoms scene as a manim-slides slide, and a deck made of them.

- class `Deck()`: The slides of a deck file, in order. ``files`` maps each slide named with its file to that file (relative to the deck file); every other slide comes from the talk's main slides file.
  - `.numbered()`: The slides that carry a footer number: those from the main file.
  - `.file_of(slide, main)`: The file ``slide`` renders from, ``main`` unless the deck names one.
- `load_deck(path)`: Read a deck file (see the module docstring).
- `cite(bib, *keys)`: The entries of ``bib`` under these keys, failing on one not in it.
- `make_footer(number, total)`: The progress bar along the bottom edge, filled to this slide's place in the deck, and the slide's number in the corner above the end of it.
- Scene `DeckSlide(Slide)`: Every slide in a deck: a Slide that stops on its finished frame, with the footer (progress bar and slide number) over everything it draws, and the references it names in CITE (keys into BIB) bottom left above it: one line each, or, if CITE holds (label, key, ...) tuples, run on together as "label: Author et al. (year)". CITE_CORNER moves it off something the footer would cover.
  - settings: `DECK`, `BIB`, `CITE`, `CITE_FORMAT`, `CITE_LABELLED_FORMAT`, `CITE_CORNER`, `SETTLE`
  - `.setup()`
  - `.cite(*keys)`: This deck's references under these keys.
  - `.citation()`
  - `.remove(*mobjects)`
- Scene `Clicks(DeckSlide)`: A DeckSlide whose beat() stops and waits for the presenter.
  - `.beat()`
- Scene `RunsOnIntoLoops(DeckSlide)`: A DeckSlide on which each stretch plays straight on into the loop after it, so a stage is one click however it is cut: the click starts the stage, and its loop holds the screen until the next. (Without auto_next the stretch would stop on its last frame and need a click of its own to start its loop.)
  - `.setup()`
  - `.loop(hold)`: Loop what hold() plays until the click, then run on into the next.
- Scene `LoopingStages(RunsOnIntoLoops)`: stage_break() loops two seconds of the running stage until the click.
  - `.stage_break()`

### `slides.player`

`src/manim_atoms/slides/player.py` — A phone-friendly web player for a rendered deck.

- `pretty(name, names=None)`: A slide's menu name: ``names[name]`` if given, else its class name in words, less the ``Slide``.
- `build_player(deck, out, sections=None, names=None, title='Slides', slides_dir=Path('slides'), first_section='Intro')`: Write the player for ``deck`` (a manim_atoms.slides.deck.Deck) to ``out``.

## bibliography

### `bibliography`

`src/manim_atoms/bibliography.py` — References from a BibTeX file, formatted as LaTeX for a slide.

- class `Name()`: One author, in BibTeX's four parts, each a tuple of words.
  - `.surname()`
  - `.render(form='initials')`: ``initials`` (C.~F.~A.~Baynham), ``last`` (Baynham) or ``full`` (Charles F.~A.~Baynham, as the bib spells the first names).
  - `.matches(spec)`: Whether this is the author ``spec`` names: a surname, optionally with a first initial after a comma ("Walker" or "Walker, T").
- class `Reference()`: One entry: its authors, and every other field as a LaTeX string.
  - `.get(name, default=None)`
- `load_bibliography(path)`: Every entry in a .bib file, by citation key. Cached until the file changes, so a re-export from Zotero is picked up.
- class `CiteFormat()`: How a reference reads: which authors, in what form, then which fields.
- `format_reference(ref, fmt=SHORT)`: One reference as a line of LaTeX, under ``fmt``.

## resources

### `resources`

`src/manim_atoms/resources.py` — Where the data shipped with the package lives.

- `data_path(*parts)`: A path under manim_atoms/data/, e.g. data_path("gw_sensitivity", "ligo.csv").
